summary: Summation No. 12 covers September 1946 in American-occupied South Korea. The month was dominated by the railroad strike of 22 September, which spread to postal, telegraph, newspaper and Seoul City Hall workers, halted transport of grain and supplies, and produced a food crisis; General Hodge's 27 September address blamed radical agitators. Military Government announced on 13 September that Korean directors would take full charge of departments, with Americans advisory, and new Civil Service classification rules took effect 30 September. Other items include the Child Labor Ordinance (No. 112), arrest orders for three Communist Party leaders, suspension of three leftist newspapers, an attempt on Syngman Rhee's life, rising cholera (14,614 cases), the opening of Seoul National University, barter trade with Japan, rationing figures, price indexes and Bank of Chosen note circulation. The report is rich in statistical charts and tables useful to economic and social historians.
highlights: On 22 September more than 30,000 railroad workers struck without prior mediation, stopping all rail transport in South Korea; on 27 September General Hodge called the strike agitator-fomented and urged a return to work and negotiation with the National Labor Mediation Board.

On 13 September the Military Governor declared that Korean directors must take full charge of their departments with Americans only advisory; Rules Number 3 of 30 September set up a civil service classification and pay system.

The arrest of Pak Heun Young, Lee Kang Kook and Lee Chu Ha, three ranking Communist Party of Southern Korea members, was ordered but not carried out; Chosen In Min Po, Hyern Dai Ilbo and Chung Ang Shin Mun were suspended and two Chung Ang editors sentenced to 18 months.

Official ration dependents reached 6,500,000 while only 88,650 metric tons of summer grain (52 percent of the pre-flood estimate) were collected; rations were 270 grams daily in Seoul and 250 elsewhere, and black-market rice hit 43 yen per pound in Seoul.

Cholera totaled 14,614 cases and 9,474 deaths by 30 September, worst in Kyongsang-namdo (1,549 cases) and Kyongsang-pukto (955); repatriation ships ran full, with 812,559 Japanese and 915,500 Koreans repatriated.
Child Labor Ordinance No. 112, effective 14 September, barred work by children 14 and under in industry and set maximum hours effective 15 February 1947.

Government-to-government barter with Japan began, with 24,000,000 yen of graphite, fluorite, talc and fresh fish shipped for coal and critical industrial goods; Bank of Chosen notes reached 11,341,307,000 yen, up 379,310,000 since August.
Seoul National University opened with 6,799 students registered by 21 September despite opposition; schools adopted a 6-6 structure and core curriculums, and 4,225,000 textbooks had been distributed.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library covers and stamps, title page for No. 12 September 1946, table of contents of four parts, and list of 37 charts, graphs and maps.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: Koreans take over departments, the 22 September rail strike, Rhee assassination attempt, grain collection shortfalls, Women's Bureau and cholera.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Military Governor's 13 September Koreanization announcement, new civil service classification, Hodge's 27 September strike address, Communist arrest orders, and Rhee assassination attempt.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Strikes cut coal and mail service; Seoul Public Utilities Board formed; 24,000,000 yen barter shipments to Japan; food crisis; Bank of Chosen notes at 11,341,307,000 yen.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Women's Bureau created, 278,905 repatriation spaces, cholera rising, 6,799 Seoul National University students, new 6-6 school system and suspension of three newspapers.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics including Hodge statements and party activity, plus legal developments, crime, police, prisons and constabulary and Coast Guard.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Legislature planning, Korean directors take charge, civil service academy and pay rules, Hodge's statements on unity and the rail strike, party conventions, and 75 registered national organizations.

sections.title: Administration and Civil Service
sections.summary: Legislature preparations, 13 September policy of Korean control, Civil Service Training Academy with 120 students and Rules Number 3 compensation plan.

sections.title: Political Affairs
sections.summary: Hodge statements on unity, the 8 September anniversary and the rail strike; Rhee's society convention, Hankook Democratic Party, Communist arrest orders, death of Hong Jin, 75 national organizations.

sections.title: Interzone Activities, Joint Commission and Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: No North-South mail in September, growing refugee flow, American delegates ready to reopen the Joint Commission, reactions to Wallace address and Chinese repatriation list.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: New revenue stamps, child labor trials, press convictions, Rhee assassination attempt on 12 September, police graduations, crime charts, prisons with 17,049 inmates, constabulary and Coast Guard.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources (crops, fisheries, coal, minerals) and commerce and industry: production, transport, communications, labor, Japan trade, rationing, prices and finance.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Rice and grain collections, Sung Duk project, fisheries output and China exports, fuel wood needs, August coal output of 26,516 tons, and mineral and smelter problems.

sections.title: Agriculture
sections.summary: Grain collections hampered by profiteering and strike, Sung Duk project 80 percent complete, 700 orchards bonded, Land Development Company dissolved, 175,408 cho of mulberry.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: Production of 3,601 tons in July and 968 in August, 44,700 kg exports to China, agar-agar capacity, 33,227 sail boats, and cloth allocated for sails.

sections.title: Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Winter fuel wood estimated at 150,000 pyong for Seoul; coal output of 26,516 tons; mineral needs, Changhang smelter, Onjin and Ilkwan mines, gold mining prohibited.

sections.title: Section 2. Commerce and Industry
sections.summary: Industry, rail and road transport, postal and telegraph services, strikes and labor law, Japan trade, food rationing and price indexes, and currency and finance.

sections.title: Industry
sections.summary: Technical and material shortages persist; paper production peaks but Hokusen newsprint mill at Kunsan faces shutdown; railway additions cost 717,000 yen; flour mills resume.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Travel restrictions lifted 30 September, rail strike stops all trains from 22 September, 17 of 33 lighthouses operating, Kyonggi Trucking Service, and Seoul Public Utilities Board.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Post office strikes at Taegu, Kyongju and Seoul, fourth mail shipment of 287 pieces to the U.S., money order figures, Cheju-do cable repair, and radio owners rising to 180,342.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Strikes by 30,000 railroad workers, telegraph and City Hall staff; Child Labor Law effective 14 September; 42,265 union members in 239 unions; employment and wage tables.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Barter with Japan: 24,000,000 yen of graphite, fluorite, talc and fish out; coal (511,504 tons Jan-Sept), locomotives, textiles and chemicals in.

sections.title: Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: 6,500,000 on rations, 88,650 tons summer grain collected, 270 gram Seoul ration, black-market rice at 43 yen, price indexes, controlled commodity distribution, and Food Regulation No. 3.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosen notes at 11,341,307,000 yen, rising loans and deposits, gold prices, and licensing of Tai Han Life Insurance Company with 10,000,000 yen capital.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, education, culture and religion, and public information, followed by the map of Korea and blank or library end pages.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Women's Bureau, repatriation totals, refugee camps with 27,657 people, medical college recognition, nursing and veterinary transfers, supply shipments, vaccine stocks, and cholera at 14,614 cases.

sections.title: Public Welfare and Repatriation
sections.summary: Welfare training institutes, Women's Bureau duties, Yonghori Leprosarium with 600 patients, 812,559 Japanese and 915,500 Koreans repatriated, and 27,657 North Korean refugees.

sections.title: Medical, Nursing, Pharmaceutical and Veterinary Affairs
sections.summary: 2,906 physicians renewed licenses, five medical colleges recognized, child mortality of 180 per thousand in first year, Pusan nursing institute, and veterinary work transferred to Koreans.

sections.title: Supply
sections.summary: Final 20,000,000 yen Civil Affairs Division medical allocation, 1,000,000 vitamin pills, 300 tons UNRRA clothing at Inchon, and biological production tables for human and veterinary vaccines.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine
sections.summary: Water plant survey, DDT spraying at Pusan, cholera at 14,614 cases and 9,474 deaths, communicable disease charts, typhus campaign begun in Seoul 16 September.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Seoul National University opens with 6,799 students, 6-6 school system and core curriculums, 4,225,000 textbooks, Chu-suk festival, 4-H vote in Kyonggi-do, and missionary returns.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Seoul National University registration and opposition, teacher resignations, school construction shortages, new 6-6 structure, core curriculum tables and textbook distribution.

sections.title: Culture, Athletics and Religion
sections.summary: Chu-suk festival on 10 September, 4-H vote with 229,367 households in favor, Girl Scout leader school at Ewha, Olympic planning committee, and 22 returned missionaries.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Campaigns on the Child Labor Ordinance and rice collection, film releases, new Culture Hour radio program, suspension of three leftist newspapers, and press comment on food and political unity.

sections.title: Information Programs, Motion Pictures and Radio
sections.summary: Child labor publicity, black-market campaign, Labor Information Party in Chungchong-namdo, eleven films released, Culture Hour and Workers' Song broadcasts.

sections.title: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Military Governor's 17 September free press statement, suspension of Chosun In Min-Po and two others, press comment on legislature, food, Wallace resignation and Korean takeover.

sections.title: Map of Korea and end pages
sections.summary: Map of Korea on page 97 followed by blank scans, library due-date card and back cover.
